reports/m03e_milestone.md says the zero-income event may contain multiple labor realizations. Basic.lean defines effective income as an affine function with strictly positive wage, so that event contains at most one labor value. This descriptive error does not affect the theorem's correctly specified event or its probability argument.

A local definition would remove this notation ambiguity; the Lean proof and final beta*p*R bound have the correct discount factors.
